record.title: Cognizant reports a 75M transformer reached about 76% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 public evaluation tasks
record.summary: A September 21, 2026 Cognizant AI Lab post and linked public repository describe a 75-million-parameter autoregressive transformer trained from scratch for ARC-AGI. Cognizant reports about 76% pass@2 on the public ARC-AGI-1 evaluation set after a little over four hours of training and evaluation on one NVIDIA H100; an eight-model ensemble reportedly reaches about 80%. The post also reports about 17% on ARC-AGI-2 for one model and about 22% for the ensemble, while a faster approximately 17-minute configuration reaches about 44% on ARC-AGI-1. The repository says headline scores average multiple seeds, but its example pages show best-seed results among eight. These are first-party reported results on public evaluation tasks, not a private leaderboard result or an independent reproduction. The linked code and evaluation recipe were inspected at the README level but not executed or audited.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Cognizant published a report and its author linked a public MIT-licensed repository for a 75M-parameter ARC-AGI-specialized autoregressive transformer.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Cognizant reports about 76% pass@2 on the ARC-AGI-1 public evaluation set after a little over four hours of training plus evaluation on one NVIDIA H100; it reports about 80% for an eight-model ensemble, approximately 17%/22% on ARC-AGI-2 for one model/ensemble, and about 44% for a faster approximately 17-minute ARC-AGI-1 configuration.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The report says scores are from the public evaluation set, not ARC-AGI’s private leaderboard. The repository says headline scores average multiple seeds, while example pages display best-seed scores among eight. No independent reproduction or code audit was performed.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent reproduction of the reported ARC-AGI-1/2 scores and training times has not been found or performed.
Exact score aggregation, uncertainty across seeds and parity of the public evaluation harness with ARC Prize reporting remain unresolved.
The public report does not provide a matched frontier-model comparison with identical test-time candidate budget and total training-plus-inference cost.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, the reported result would materially affect compute and architecture choices for narrow, structured reasoning tasks by showing that a small from-scratch model can attain a high public ARC-AGI-1 score with modest single-GPU time. The importance is notable but bounded to ARC tasks and the provider’s public evaluation; transfer, score integrity and comparison parity remain unverified.
limitations: All benchmark scores and compute times are first-party claims; code was not run and no independent reproduction was performed.
Evaluation is on ARC-AGI public evaluation tasks, not the private leaderboard; the author describes them as estimates and cautions that comparisons depend on evaluation settings and cost accounting.

The report compares score ranges with much larger models, but the tasks, prompting, test-time procedure and training scope are not matched to general frontier systems. This is not evidence of broad capability parity.
The repository README says headline results average multiple seeds; linked example pages show best-seed outputs among eight. The exact summary aggregation and variance were not reconstructed here.

The benchmark contains evaluation demonstrations in the ARC-related training data while held-out test outputs are excluded according to the report/repository; no independent contamination audit was performed.
The 17-minute configuration reaches about 44%, showing a material score-compute tradeoff; 76% should not be presented as the result of the faster recipe.

technical.claimed_result: Cognizant reports about 76% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 public evaluation with a 75M model after a little over four hours of training and evaluation on one H100; about 80% for eight models; about 17%/22% on ARC-AGI-2; and about 44% for a faster 17-minute configuration.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public report and README specify the model size, task-specific method, public evaluation scope and runnable recipe. The source and README were inspected; code was not executed or audited, so reported scores and timing remain claims.
technical.mechanism: The model preserves row/column/grid identity through coordinate representations, augments color/rotation/reflection/scale, predicts multiple tokens ahead, generates transformed candidate solutions and ranks them with augmented likelihood plus symbolic consistency checks.
technical.regime: 75M parameters, trained from scratch on ARC-related data; ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 public evaluation tasks; one-H100 full recipe (>4h), faster recipe (~17 min), and eight independently trained models for ensemble. The result excludes held-out test outputs according to the authors; evaluation demonstrations are included in ARC-related training data.
technical.reproducibility: A public MIT-licensed repository provides source layout, data preparation and run instructions. Its README was inspected but code, dependencies, datasets, checkpoints and scoring were not executed or independently audited.
technical.strongest_baseline: The post compares the ARC-AGI-1 public-set estimate with reported large-model scores, while noting different capabilities and cost accounting. No matched model, prompt, candidate-budget, training-cost and scoring-harness control is established.

brief.title: Cognizant reports a 75M transformer reached about 76% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 public evaluation tasks
brief.why_it_matters: The report is a concrete case where a task-structured 75M model and four hours of single-GPU work are claimed to reach a high ARC-AGI-1 public-set score. If independently reproduced under a clean split, this would inform how much specialized representation, augmentation, multi-token prediction and candidate selection can substitute for broad pretraining on one structured reasoning benchmark. It does not show general reasoning parity with frontier models: ARC-AGI-2 scores are lower, the evaluation is public-set only, and no matched direct baseline or independent run was established.
